identity.title: Optimal and Scalable MAPF via Multi-Marginal Optimal Transport and Schrödinger Bridges

problem.claim: Solve anonymous multi-agent path finding, where robots travel between targets on a finite connected graph.

contributions.claim: Recasts MAPF as a Markovian multi-marginal optimal transport problem whose exponential formulation collapses to a polynomial-size linear program.
For the anonymous setting, identifies conditions yielding feasibility, total unimodularity, and minimum-cost integral transports without space-time overlap.
Introduces a Schrödinger-bridge formulation with an iterative Sinkhorn-type solver and uses its fractional transport as a template for a reduced LP.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, under stated conditions, the LP produces minimum-cost integral non-overlapping transports.
Under standard assumptions, the authors report that the Schrödinger-bridge formulation reduces to entropic MMOT regularization solvable by Sinkhorn-type iterations.

The authors report extensive experiments highlighting optimality and scalability, and describe the reduced-LP approach as producing near-optimal integral transports with substantially lower complexity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Anonymous MAPF is posed as moving robots to targets on a finite connected graph.
MAPF is connected to Markovian MMOT, enabling a polynomial-size LP representation.
Conditions are given for feasible, totally unimodular LPs with minimum-cost integral transports that avoid space-time overlap.
Schrödinger bridges provide an entropic, Sinkhorn-solvable formulation and a fractional template for a reduced LP; experiments are reported to support optimality and scalability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each modeling transformation with a distinct computational or structural consequence: polynomial LP size, integrality, and iterative scalability.

lessons.interpretation: Separating formulation, guarantees, and solver consequences makes a technical contribution easier to audit.
lessons.application: Organize a paper's abstract by pairing each proposed representation with the precise property or algorithmic benefit it enables.
lessons.exception: This structure is less suitable when the work has one tightly coupled result and no meaningful intermediate consequences.

source_observation.claim: The abstract distinguishes fractional Schrödinger-bridge output from the subsequent reduced-LP construction of integral transports.

lessons.interpretation: Explicitly labeling intermediate objects prevents readers from confusing a relaxed solution with the final feasible output.
lessons.application: When using relaxations, state which stage produces the relaxed object and which later stage restores the required discrete constraints.
lessons.exception: Do not imply restoration of exact feasibility or optimality unless the relevant conditions and evidence are supplied.

unknowns: The standard assumptions behind the Schrödinger-bridge reduction are not specified.
The abstract does not quantify the reported near-optimality, complexity reduction, or experimental comparisons.
Instance sizes, baselines, and detailed conditions for LP feasibility and integrality are omitted.
